topic: The Fundamental Bridge: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Tangent vs. The Area
lecture_lines: Calculus explores two core concepts: derivatives and integrals.
Derivatives analyze the slope of a curve locally.
Integrals calculate the total area accumulated under curves.
animations: Show a tangent line mobject and an area integral mobject on opposite sides.
Label Tangent in #FFD700 and Area in #00BFFF.

sections.title: The Inverse Mechanism: Cancellation
lecture_lines: Integration and differentiation act as inverse processes.
Differentiating then integrating returns the original function.
This relationship is like undoing an action.
animations: Show a function f(x) and its integral F(x).
Display the formula F(x) = \int f(t) dt in #FFFFFF.
Apply d/dx operator to F(x) using #FF4500 to show cancellation.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Visualization)
lecture_lines: Define A(x) as the accumulated area bucket.
As x grows, the area bucket increases.
The rate of change is the function's height.
Area accumulation links directly to function values.
The Fundamental Theorem connects these two ideas.
animations: Draw a function plot f(x) in #FFFFFF.
Sweep an area rectangle A(x) from left to right.
Highlight the height of the rectangle with #FFD700.
Label the vertical slice f(x) at x.
Animate the derivative A'(x) = f(x) in #00FF00.

sections.title: Practical Application & Summary
lecture_lines: Know the rate of change to reconstruct accumulation.
The anti-derivative recovers the original total amount.
Calculus provides a path from rates to totals.
Explorer Alex tracks speed to find total distance.
This completes our Fundamental Theorem of Calculus summary.
animations: Show a summary table with Rate (f) and Total (F) columns.
Highlight the fundamental theorem F'(x) = f(x) in #FFFFFF.
Fade out all elements to clear the screen.
